headline: Navigating the Largest Wilderness in America
reservation: The park does not require an entry fee or permit for day hiking, but the primary bottleneck is McCarthy Road access and deep-park lodging. Shuttles, guided glacier treks, and Kennecott Mill tours require advanced booking due to the extremely short summer season. Always verify road status and flightseeing availability with official operators before departure.

days.title: Copper River Orientation

stops.name: Copper Center Visitor Complex
stops.detail: Review topographic maps and watch the park film to understand the scale of the Wrangell Range.

stops.name: Liberty Falls State Recreation Site
stops.detail: Take a short hike near the cascading water before starting the journey toward Chitina.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for paved transit to Chitina; conditions vary
days.note: This is the final location for reliable fuel and grocery supplies before the McCarthy Road.

days.title: The Historic Railway Route

stops.name: Kuskulana River Bridge
stops.detail: Cross a high-span historic bridge for dizzying views of the canyon and river below.

stops.name: Gilahina Trestle
stops.detail: Observe the massive wooden ruins of the railway era and stretch your legs on the short trail.

days.driving: Allow 3 to 4 hours for the 60-mile McCarthy Road; conditions vary significantly
days.note: The road is unpaved and built on an old railway bed; high-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended.

days.title: Glacial Ice and Industrial History

stops.name: Kennecott Mill Town
stops.detail: Tour the 14-story copper concentration mill and explore the historic red buildings of the landmark.

stops.name: Root Glacier Trail
stops.detail: Hike the lateral moraine for views of the white and blue ice of the Root Glacier.

days.driving: Walking and local shuttle transfers only; no private vehicles allowed in Kennecott
days.note: Glacier trekking requires specialized gear; check with local guide services for equipment and safety.

days.title: St. Elias Alpine Vistas

stops.name: Bagley Icefield Flightseeing
stops.detail: View the massive 'conveyor belt' glaciers and 16,000-foot peaks from the air.

stops.name: Bonanza Mine Trail
stops.detail: Tackle a strenuous uphill hike to see mine ruins perched high above the Kennicott Valley.

days.driving: Walking and local transfer only; flight times are weather dependent
days.note: Alpine weather can change rapidly; always carry layers even on sunny mornings.

intel.title: Kennicott River Terminus
intel.text: Private vehicles must park at the end of McCarthy Road before the footbridge. Fees apply at private lots, and space is limited during peak July weekends.

intel.title: End-of-Road Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent for most of the McCarthy Road and very limited in McCarthy town. Satellite communication devices are recommended for backcountry safety.

intel.title: Last Reliable Pump
intel.text: Chitina is the final fuel stop before the 120-mile round trip on McCarthy Road. Ensure your vehicle has a full-sized spare tire as historic railroad spikes can cause punctures.

intel.title: The Three-Hour Sixty
intel.text: Though only 60 miles, the McCarthy Road involves washboard surfaces and narrow bridges. Allow a minimum of three hours each way to avoid vehicle damage.

intel.title: Footbridge Crossing
intel.text: Access to McCarthy and Kennecott is via a pedestrian footbridge. Budget time for the local shuttle or a 0.5-mile walk to town after parking your vehicle.

plan.arrival: Fly into Gulkana or drive from Anchorage; secure all backcountry food and gear in Glennallen before proceeding to Chitina.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD vehicles are recommended for McCarthy Road; check rental contracts as many prohibit travel on this specific unpaved route.
plan.goldenHour: The Kennecott Mill provides a dramatic subject as light hits the red facades, though the surrounding peaks may shade the valley early.
